questions.stem: Three parallel glass slabs of refractive indices 1.5, sqrt(3) and 1.5 respectively have widths 2 mm, 1 mm and 4 mm, combination in air; light incident on first slab at angle of incidence pi/3 -- angle w.r.t. normal at which light emerges from the final surface?

Three wires X, Y and Z of the same length, ratio of conductivities 1 : 2 : 3; cross-sectional area of Z is twice that of Y and resistance of X equals resistance of Z -- ratio of the resistance of Y to that of X?

Two point charges of 4 C and 16 C kept 0.18 m apart; a third point charge of 1 C kept between them so that the potential energy of the system is minimum -- magnitude of the electric field at the 1 C charge?

Consider the following statements in respect of sound waves: I. speed decreases with an increase in temperature if atmospheric pressure remains the same; II. speed increases with increasing humidity if atmospheric pressure remains the same; III. speed is not affected by a change in atmospheric pressure, provided the temperature is kept constant. Which of the statements given above are correct?

Statement-I: Marine animals remain alive in winter and move near the bottom of lakes despite frozen water on the surface. Statement-II: The density of water is maximum at 4 degrees C and water at the bottom of lakes remains warm in winter. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.

options.label: C
options.text: Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is not correct.

options.label: D
options.text: Statement-I is not correct, but Statement-II is correct.

questions.stem: A bicycle racing track is a level circular road of radius 10 m; three cyclists P, Q and R with identical cycles cycling at 2 m/s, 3 m/s and 5 m/s; coefficient of friction between tyres and road is 0.1 -- which cyclist will slip? (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
The bob of a simple pendulum is displaced from its mean position and released from rest 0.20 m above its mean position -- speed of the bob as it passes through the mean position? (Take g = 10 m/s^2)

A tennis ball of mass 350 g is thrown vertically upwards at a speed of 4 m/s; M is the maximum gravitational potential energy and H the maximum height -- which one of the following is correct? (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
Which of the following is correct regarding the total internal reflection at the interface between two different optical media?

options.label: A
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing at any angle from a medium of low refractive index to a medium of high refractive index.

options.label: B
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing from a medium of high refractive index to a medium of low refractive index and at an angle greater than the critical angle.

options.label: C
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing at any angle from a medium of high refractive index to a medium of low refractive index.

options.label: D
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing from a medium of low refractive index to a medium of high refractive index and at an angle greater than the critical angle.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements: I. The weight of an object is the same everywhere on the surface of the Earth, but its inertial mass could be different; II. The inertial mass and gravitational mass of an object are proportional and the proportionality constant is the same everywhere; III. The inertial mass and weight of an object are the same at different places on Earth. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following: I. Gravitational field due to a spherical body; II. Electrostatic field due to a point charge; III. Strong nuclear force field due to a proton; IV. Magnetic field due to a bar magnet. How many of the above follow the inverse square law?
While pouring water slowly from a jug, a general observation is that a water layer usually flows along the side of the jug -- which property of water is responsible for this phenomenon?

options.label: B
options.text: Relatively low vapour pressure at room temperature

questions.stem: A fish is at a depth d in water of refractive index 4/3; a transparent slab of refractive index 3/2 and thickness d/2 is placed on the surface of water -- apparent depth of the fish as observed by an observer in air?
A particle of mass m moves along x-direction under the force F(x) = F_0 (1 - x/L) for 0 <= x <= L; particle starts from rest at x = 0 -- speed (v) of the particle at x = L?

A narrow tunnel passes through the centre of a planet of radius R and uniform mass density rho; a particle is released into the tunnel -- angular frequency of oscillation of the particle (omega)? (Symbols carry their usual meaning)

Consider the following statements in relation to respiration in animals: I. Glucose breaks down into pyruvate in the cytoplasm of all cells in both aerobic and anaerobic conditions; II. The energy released during anaerobic respiration is greater than the energy released in aerobic respiration; III. Carbon dioxide is released only in aerobic respiration. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
In humans, the exit of partially digested food from the stomach into the small intestine is regulated by which one of the following structures/processes?
Which of the following cells form components of complex permanent tissue in plants? I. Companion cells; II. Sieve tubes; III. Tracheids; IV. Vessels. Select the answer using the code given below.
Which one of the following is **not** a part of the hindbrain of human beings?
